caption: Programmatic Credential
description: The Programmatic Credential object describes service-specific credentials used for direct API access and system integration. These credentials are typically issued by individual services or platforms for accessing their APIs and resources, focusing on credential lifecycle management and usage tracking. Examples include API keys, service account keys, client certificates, and vendor-specific access tokens.
name: programmatic_credential

created_time.description: The time the credential was created or became valid.

expiration_time.description: The time the credential expires. Credentials past this time no longer grant access, and credentials approaching it indicate rotation work.

last_used_time.description: The timestamp when this programmatic credential was last used for authentication or API access. This helps track credential usage patterns, identify dormant credentials that may pose security risks, and support credential lifecycle management. The timestamp should reflect the most recent successful authentication or API call using this credential.

name.description: The display name of the credential, if the issuing service names it. For example, the description an administrator gives a client secret.

type.description: The type of programmatic credential, normalized to the caption of the type_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

type_id.description: The normalized type of programmatic credential.

1.caption: API Key
1.description: An API key or personal access token issued by a service for direct API access.

2.caption: Client Secret
2.description: A secret or password registered for an application or client, used to authenticate the application itself.

3.caption: Certificate
3.description: A client certificate or public key registered for an application or service account.

4.caption: Access Token
4.description: A bearer or OAuth access token issued for programmatic access.

5.caption: Service Account Key
5.description: A key issued for a service account.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The credential type is not mapped. See the type attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

uid.description: The unique identifier of the programmatic credential. This could be an API key ID, service account key ID, access token identifier, certificate serial number, or other unique identifier that distinguishes this credential from others. Examples: AWS Access Key ID, GCP Service Account Key ID, Azure Application ID, or OAuth2 token identifier.
